Rather, he sent and brought the great throne that was in Tabriz,
that upon which Abagha and Arghun and the other kings who arose after them had sat,
and he set it up in the vicinity of Ujan,
and he went up and sat upon it,
and he supposed that his kingdom was henceforth established.
And after they had remained there a few days,
while occupied with eating and drinking,
they departed toward Siahkuh.
And there the sons and daughters, and brothers and kinsmen, and army commanders and all the Mongol nobles gathered in agreement.
And so Baydu began to deal with them in all humility of mind,
and to each one of the brothers and cousins he handed over a certain territory,
on the condition
that they should consume all the revenue of that territory.
And if anything was left over from them,
they should send it to Baydu;
and if they lacked anything,
they should send to him to take whatever was sufficient for their maintenance.

And so all the royal sons and nobles were dismissed from his presence with joy and gladness and cheerfulness, while praising God for the peace and harmony that had been brought about among all the armies and nobles of the Mongols.
Now Ghazan, when he arrived in the vicinity of Siahkuh,
learned that Baydu had snatched the kingdom for himself,
and sat upon the throne of the kingdom unlawfully.
Then he burned with wrath,
and was enraged,
and was exceedingly grieved,
because all his labor and weariness and the toil of the long road, which had befallen him and the armies that were with him, had appeared vain and empty.
And he accused Baydu, saying:
"Why did he call me? And having called me,
why did he not wait until I reached him,
and sit upon the throne with my agreement?" But Baydu was confident
that with humility of mind and generous gifts he could appease the mind of Ghazan,
and that he would hand over to him all of Khorasan, Shiraz, Bahrain, and Kirman,
and also give him all the camps of his father Arghun,
and not keep with himself even one of them,
but would hand over all of them, along with their people, horses, herds, droves, possessions, and property to him,
so that he might take them and return to Khorasan.
